passage: Tanvir's diary, Tuesday night. Damini told our manager today that the wrong figures in the sales report were mine. In front of everyone. My face went hot and I wanted to snap back, "You entered those numbers!" I didn't. I said, "I can check." At my desk I opened the file history. The change was made on Monday from her login. I printed it. I am not going to accuse her tomorrow. I will show the manager the record and ask how we fix the report. Part of me still wants revenge, and I am going to sleep on that instead of acting. 😔 Tanvir

qa.q: When was the change made to the sales report?
qa.a: The change was made on Monday from Damini's login.

qa.q: What did Tanvir feel and want when Damini blamed Tanvir?
qa.a: Tanvir felt angry and embarrassed, face going hot and wanting to snap back, but held it in and offered to check.

qa.q: What is Tanvir's plan for tomorrow, and why is it a good one?
qa.a: Tanvir will show the manager the printed record and ask how to fix the report, which relies on facts rather than accusing or retaliating.

qa.q: How might Damini see the moment when the record is shown?
qa.a: Damini may feel exposed or defensive, which is why Tanvir plans to focus on fixing the report instead of blaming.

grounding: A colleague blames Tanvir for a mistake; Tanvir stays calm, presents facts and involves the manager.

passage:
Jaya: siami, manager's asking why the aizawl order went out late. i said you had the dispatch sheet
Lalremsiami: hi jaya. i didn't have it, you did. you took it on thursday for the address change
Jaya: are you sure? i thought i gave it back
Lalremsiami: i'm sure. here's your message from thursday: "taking the dispatch sheet, will return by 3"
Lalremsiami: it came back to my desk on monday
Jaya: oh. ok. i forgot
Lalremsiami: i'm not angry. but i can't let this sit as my mistake. can we both tell mr lalthanga at 2?
Jaya: yeah. sorry. i panicked when he asked
Lalremsiami: happens. we'll say what happened and suggest a sign-out book for the sheet
Jaya: that's a good idea actually
Jaya: thanks for not blasting me in the group
Lalremsiami: 🙂 see you at 2

qa.q: When did Jaya take the dispatch sheet?
qa.a: On Thursday, for the address change.

qa.q: How does Lalremsiami seem to feel, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Calm and firm: "i'm not angry", yet unwilling to let the mistake sit, replying with facts instead of accusations.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do instead of retaliating?
qa.a: Showed Jaya's own Thursday message, proposed telling the manager together at 2, and suggested a sign-out book.

qa.q: How does Jaya feel once shown the message?
qa.a: Embarrassed and sorry, admitting to panicking, and grateful not to be blasted in the group.

grounding: Shows being blamed for a colleague's mistake and responding calmly with facts and involving the manager rather than retaliating.

passage:
At the milk-collection centre in Anand district, forty litres had gone sour overnight. When the supervisor, Patel-kaka, asked who had closed the chiller, Mehak said quickly, "Sahil was last out."
Sahil felt heat climb his neck. He had left at six; Mehak had stayed till eight to count the evening cans. He knew about her unpaid tea-stall tab too, and her late mornings. It would be easy to fling all of it back.
He didn't. He took a breath. "Kaka, can we check the logbook?"
The logbook showed his signature at 6:05 and hers at 8:10, with the chiller temperature noted by her at the end. It had been set two degrees too high.
Mehak looked at the floor. "I thought I'd set it right."
"It happens," Sahil said quietly. "Maybe we both sign the temperature from now on?"
Patel-kaka nodded and wrote a new rule on the board: two signatures at closing. At the gate later, Mehak said, "Sorry." He nodded. That was enough.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling when Mehak blamed him?
qa.a: Angry, with heat climbing his neck, and tempted to throw her other slips back at her.

qa.q: How did Sahil handle the false blame?
qa.a: He stayed calm, asked the supervisor to check the logbook, let the facts speak, and suggested two signatures at closing.

qa.q: How did Mehak feel when the logbook was checked?
qa.a: Ashamed, looking at the floor, and later sorry.

grounding: Illustrates being falsely blamed by a colleague, and staying calm, presenting facts and involving the supervisor instead of retaliating.
